entries.answer_en: I am an AI and software engineer with more than 15 years of work. I started with payment systems in Kuwait, running kiosk and POS projects. Then I moved to AI at Al Najat: early-warning, helpdesk classification, and a donation kiosk with Whisper and TTS. Since 2023 I work at Jordan’s Ministry of Education on BTEC. There I build RAG and multi-agent tools for student assessment support, automated feedback, and exam questions, plus similarity checking and completion risk monitoring. I studied computer engineering, and I hold PMP and PRINCE2.
entries.followup_en: The Ministry work started in 2023. That is where LLM, RAG, and the question flow live. Production orchestration is plain Python. LangChain was only a test, and LangGraph is not in production. At Al Najat, from 2017 to 2023, I built a Whisper kiosk. I also built an early-warning tool with Pandas and sklearn, and helpdesk sorting with TF-IDF. From 2010 to 2017 at VNC I ran KNET payment kiosks and POS. I am PMP certified.

entries.answer_en: Since 2023 I am a Systems Developer and AI Engineer for BTEC at Jordan’s Ministry of Education. I build and maintain the software systems that support BTEC educational and administrative processes. That includes the core process software for units, assessments, and school follow-up, plus AI tools on top of it: student assessment support, automated feedback, and exam question generation with RAG and a multi-agent workflow; an assignment similarity checker with embeddings and cosine similarity; and BTEC completion risk monitoring with SQL, Pandas, and Scikit-learn.
entries.followup_en: For the generative tools the pattern is: prepare BTEC content, chunk it, embed it, store it in a vector database, retrieve with RAG, then agents for retrieve, analyze, and generate. Similarity has no LLM. Completion risk is classic data and ML. I own the AI design and work with Ministry IT on access and deployment.

entries.answer_en: BTEC (Business and Technology Education Council) is a vocational qualification in the UK. It focuses on practical, work-related learning. In Jordan, the Ministry of Education adopted BTEC for vocational education. It includes units, learning outcomes, and assessments.

entries.answer_en:
I developed an AI system to help teachers generate BTEC exam and assessment questions based on BTEC assessment criteria.

When a teacher selects a topic or BTEC assessment criteria, the system analyzes the relevant content and creates questions based on the selected topic and criteria.

I prepared the BTEC learning content, split it into smaller chunks, created embeddings, and stored them in a vector database.

I built the RAG workflow to retrieve the most relevant BTEC criteria and learning content for the selected topic.

I also used a multi-agent workflow to manage the process. One agent retrieves the relevant BTEC content, another agent analyzes the selected topic and assessment criteria, and a third agent generates the questions.

I tested the generated questions, checked accuracy, and improved the prompts.
entries.followup_en: This is for teachers generating exam and assessment questions. Student assessment support and automated feedback are separate projects with the same RAG and three-agent pattern, but different outputs.
entries.answer_ar: طورت نظام ذكاء اصطناعي لمساعدة المعلمين على توليد أسئلة امتحان وتقييم BTEC وفق معايير التقييم. عندما يختار المعلم موضوعاً أو معايير، يحلّل النظام المحتوى ويُنشئ الأسئلة. حضّرت محتوى BTEC وقسّمته إلى أجزاء وأنشأت تضمينات وخزّنتها في قاعدة متجهات. بنيت سير عمل RAG، واستخدمت ثلاثة وكلاء: استرجاع، وتحليل الموضوع والمعايير، وتوليد الأسئلة، مع اختبار الدقة وتحسين الـ prompts.

entries.answer_en: I split the work into steps so each part is clear and testable. First retrieve the relevant BTEC content. Then analyze the topic, criteria, or student work. Then generate the questions, feedback, or assessment report. That multi-agent split keeps retrieval separate from generation, so I can check what text went into the model.
entries.followup_en: If retrieval returns the wrong unit text, I fix retrieval. If the draft is weak, I fix the analyze or generate prompts. One giant prompt hides which step failed. For official BTEC material that separation matters.
entries.answer_ar: قسّمت العمل إلى خطوات قابلة للفحص: استرجاع محتوى BTEC، ثم تحليل الموضوع أو عمل الطالب، ثم توليد الأسئلة أو التغذية الراجعة أو تقرير التقييم. فصل الاسترجاع عن التوليد يوضح مصدر الخطأ.

entries.answer_en: I started with an external LLM API for a fast proof of concept. Student personal data never went to the model. Curriculum text can go in. Names stay inside our system, linked by internal IDs. Every model call goes through one internal interface, so we can change the model later.
entries.followup_en: I split content by sensitivity. Unit text is low sensitivity. Student identity is high. After the model returns, our system maps the ID back to a name for the teacher screen. The interface is one setting, not a rewrite. That is also how I would move to a self-hosted model. I do not hard-code a vendor into the business logic.

I developed an AI system to help teachers review and assess student work based on BTEC assessment criteria.

When a student submits an assignment, the system analyzes the work and generates a report showing strengths, weaknesses, achieved criteria, and areas that need improvement.

I prepared the BTEC learning content, split it into smaller chunks, created embeddings, and stored them in a vector database.

I built the RAG workflow to retrieve the most relevant BTEC criteria and learning content for the student’s assignment.

I also used a multi-agent workflow to manage the process. One agent retrieves the relevant BTEC content, another agent analyzes the student’s work, and a third agent generates the assessment report.

I also tested the results, checked the accuracy of the assessment, and improved the prompts.
entries.followup_en: This is Ministry BTEC work for teachers. It uses RAG and a three-agent flow: retrieve, analyze, generate. It is not the similarity checker, and it is not classic ML like early-warning.

entries.answer_en:
I developed an AI system to help teachers identify high similarity between BTEC student assignments.

The system analyzes and compares student assignments to find similar content that may need additional review.

I prepared and cleaned the assignment text and created embeddings to represent the text numerically.

I used cosine similarity to compare the embeddings and calculate the similarity score between assignments.

The system highlights assignments with high similarity for teacher review.

I also tested the results, checked the similarity scores, and adjusted the similarity threshold when needed.
entries.followup_en: This is not an LLM and not RAG. There is no generation step. Embeddings and cosine similarity only flag pairs. The teacher decides what to do next.
entries.answer_ar: طورت نظام ذكاء اصطناعي لمساعدة المعلمين على اكتشاف التشابه العالي بين واجبات طلاب BTEC. يحلّل النظام الواجبات ويقارنها لإيجاد محتوى متشابه قد يحتاج مراجعة إضافية. حضّرت نص الواجب ونظّفته وأنشأت تضمينات، واستخدمت تشابه جيب التمام لحساب الدرجة، ثم أُبرزت الحالات للمراجعة، مع اختبار النتائج وضبط عتبة التشابه عند الحاجة.

entries.answer_en: I did not pick a textbook number. Teachers had already reviewed some pairs: real follow-up cases, and expected overlap like shared question text. I tried different cutoffs and looked at misses and false alarms. Too low and teachers ignore the tool. Too high and we miss real copies. So they still decide.
entries.followup_en: Shared assignment instructions score high even when the student work is honest. Metadata filters reduce that noise before the score. I cared more about a list teachers would actually open than about a pretty chart. The cutoff can move by subject if needed. I would not freeze one global number forever.

entries.answer_en: No, it is vector search and comparison: embeddings, similarity, and metadata filters. Those blocks also appear in RAG. It becomes RAG when a language model writes from the retrieved text. We did not do that. The teacher reads the two passages.
entries.followup_en: An LLM summary of the match would start to look like RAG. We avoided that because the case is about a student. I wanted the evidence on screen, not a generated accusation. Retrieval without generation is still useful. I keep the names clean so the interview and the architecture stay honest.
entries.answer_ar: ليس RAG. هو بحث متجهات ومقارنة بلا توليد. RAG يبدأ عندما يكتب النموذج من النصوص المسترجعة.

entries.answer_en: Long papers were a problem, because one vector per assignment hid a copied paragraph, so I moved to chunks. Shared question text also looks similar even when work is honest, so filters and a tuned cutoff helped. Trust was the last issue: if the tool accuses students, teachers walk away.
entries.followup_en: I show the two passages side by side with the score. I never write a guilt label. Arabic and English mix in some assignments, which makes naive word matching worse and is another reason embeddings helped. I also had to extract text cleanly from messy files before any vector was computed. Garbage in still beats a fancy model.

entries.question: Why Random Forest?
aliases: why random forest
entries.answer_en: Random Forest works well with tables. It takes mixed data types. One strange value does not break it. And it shows which features mattered, so I could explain a score to a teacher.
entries.answer_ar: Random Forest يتعامل مع أنواع البيانات المختلطة، وقوي ضد القيم الشاذة، ويوفر أهمية الميزات، ويؤدي بشكل جيد على البيانات الجدولية. كان أيضًا قابلاً للتفسير بدرجة كافية للمعلمين.

entries.question: Why Linear SVM?
aliases: why linear svm
entries.answer_en: Linear SVM works well with text, because text turns into many features. It also holds up on a small dataset and does not overfit easily.
entries.answer_ar: Linear SVM يعمل بشكل جيد للبيانات النصية عالية الأبعاد وقوي ضد الإفراط في التعلم. يؤدي أيضًا بشكل جيد مع مجموعات البيانات الصغيرة.

entries.question: Why Gradient Boosting?
aliases: why gradient boosting
entries.answer_en: Gradient Boosting handles tabular data well, captures non-linear relationships, and provides feature importance. It also performed better than Logistic Regression in cross-validation.
entries.answer_ar: Gradient Boosting يتعامل مع البيانات الجدولية بشكل جيد، ويلتقط العلاقات غير الخطية، ويوفر أهمية الميزات. أدى أيضًا بشكل أفضل من Logistic Regression في التحقق المتقاطع.

entries.question: What problems did you face in the early-warning project?
aliases: what problems did you face in the early warning project
what was difficult about building the early warning model
what challenges came up in the early warning model
hardest technical problem in the early warning model
entries.answer_en: Three things. Most students were fine, so the classes were unbalanced and accuracy looked good while the model missed the students who mattered. Time was the second: I had to predict early in the term, so a random split would have leaked final grades. Third, teachers asked why a name was on the list, so a black box was not an option.
entries.followup_en: I handled each one. For the imbalance I looked at recall for the students who needed help, and I watched precision so the list stayed short. For time I split the data in term order, and I dropped any column that only exists after the result. For trust I started with a simple model that people can explain, and every score came with its reasons. Missing attendance was itself a sign, so I flagged it instead of filling the average.
entries.answer_ar: ثلاثة أمور. أغلب الطلاب بخير، فالفئات غير متوازنة، والدقة تبدو عالية بينما النموذج يفوّت الطلاب المهمين. والثاني الزمن: التنبؤ مبكراً في الفصل، فالتقسيم العشوائي كان سيسرّب الدرجات النهائية. والثالث أن المعلمين يسألون لماذا ظهر هذا الاسم، فالصندوق الأسود لم يكن خياراً.

entries.answer_en: I built it. I joined grades and attendance in Pandas. I chose the features. I wrote the sklearn pipeline and picked the metric. Then I gave teachers a sorted list, with the reasons behind each score. They tested it on real cases and chose the support. I did not give the model work to anyone else.
entries.followup_en: The choices were mine. Recall as the main metric. A simple model that people can explain, not a neural net. A split by time, not random. And a flag for missing attendance, instead of filling the average. The part I did not own is the action. The model says who to look at first. The teacher decides what to do. I said that from day one, so nobody read the list as a final answer.
entries.answer_ar: أنا بنيته. دمجت الدرجات والحضور في Pandas، واخترت الخصائص، وكتبت pipeline في sklearn، وحددت المقياس، وأنتجت قائمة المتابعة المرتّبة مع العوامل وراء كل درجة. المعلمون جرّبوه على حالات حقيقية وقرروا نوع الدعم. لم أسند النمذجة لأحد.

entries.question: What problems did you face in the completion risk project?
aliases: what problems did you face in the completion risk project
what was difficult in completion risk monitoring
what challenges came up in the completion risk work
hardest part of completion risk monitoring
entries.answer_en: The main one was that people mixed two different questions. How complete a school is today is arithmetic. Whether it will finish on time is a forecast, and a forecast needs past terms. For some units the history was thin, so I did not build a clever model on top of nothing. The second problem was definitions: two people counted completion differently until the rule lived in SQL.
entries.followup_en: Where there was enough history, I used sklearn for the risk part only. Where there was not, I gave the number and said there is no base for a forecast. Putting the joins and the rule in SQL meant everyone saw the same number. That matters in a ministry, because a list turns into a school visit. There is no LLM and no retrieval in that pipeline.
entries.answer_ar: الأهم أن الناس كانت تخلط سؤالين مختلفين. نسبة الإنجاز اليوم حساب، واحتمال الإنجاز في الموعد تنبؤ، والتنبؤ يحتاج فصولاً سابقة. في بعض الوحدات كان التاريخ ضعيفاً، فلم أبنِ نموذجاً ذكياً فوق لا شيء. والمشكلة الثانية التعريفات: كل شخص يحسب الإنجاز بطريقة، حتى وضعت القاعدة داخل SQL.

entries.question: What was your role in the completion risk project?
aliases: what was your role in the completion risk project

your responsibility in completion risk monitoring
entries.answer_en: I wrote it from start to end. The SQL that pulls the school and unit records and the exact counts. The cleaning in Pandas. The rule for completion. And the sklearn part for risk, where history allowed it. The output was a follow-up list with the main signs. The Ministry chose which schools to visit.
entries.followup_en: The choice I defend is keeping the math and the guess apart. If I can calculate a number, I calculate it. I do not ask a model to guess it. I also kept the rules in SQL, not in a notebook. So the same query gives the same count next term, and after I leave. FastAPI can serve the list later, but that was not the hard part.
entries.answer_ar: كتبته من البداية إلى النهاية. استعلامات SQL التي تسحب سجلات المدارس والوحدات والأعداد الدقيقة، والتنظيف في Pandas، وقاعدة احتساب الإنجاز، وجزء sklearn لجانب المخاطرة حيث توفّر تاريخ. المخرج قائمة متابعة مع مؤشرات، والوزارة تقرر أي مدارس تزور.

entries.answer_en: I built the voice side. I ran Whisper on the machine, so the audio stayed there. I cleaned the noise. I used voice detection, so it did not record all the time. I trained a small model to pick a male or female reply voice. And I wrote the NLP step that sent the request to the right place. The image functions sat on the same kiosk.
entries.followup_en: Most of the accuracy came from clean audio, and from knowing when the person stopped talking. It did not come from a bigger model. That was my call. The privacy rule was mine too: keep the text, do not keep the audio. This was 2017 to 2023, before my LLM work. There is no LLM in that path, and I do not call it one.
entries.answer_ar: بنيت الجانب الصوتي. تشغيل Whisper محلياً ليبقى الصوت داخل الجهاز، وتنظيف الضوضاء، واكتشاف النشاط الصوتي بدل التسجيل المستمر، والمصنّف الصغير الذي يختار صوت الرد ذكراً أو أنثى، وخطوة NLP التي توجّه الطلب. ووظائف معالجة الصور كانت على الجهاز نفسه.

entries.question: What problems did you face in the KNET payment projects?
aliases: what problems did you face in the knet payment projects
what was difficult in the kuwait payment work
what challenges came up in the pos and kiosk payment projects
hardest part of the vnc payment projects
entries.answer_en: A payment must not stop, and it must not charge twice. That is harder than it sounds. We had kiosks, POS machines, the national network, and ministry systems. When something broke, it was never clean. A payment would time out in the middle, and the two sides would not agree on what happened. So the work was logs, matching records, testing with real edge cases, and vendors who had to fix their side.
entries.followup_en: The habit I kept is simple. I build as if someone will read the log tomorrow and ask what happened. That is the same reason I store the retrieved text and ask for teacher approval in the Ministry work. Keeping the service running was the job, not the demo. A nice screen that charges twice is a failure. An ugly one that matches records is not.
entries.answer_ar: الدفعة يجب ألا تتوقف وألا تُحسب مرتين. وهذا أصعب مما يبدو عبر أجهزة الخدمة الذاتية ونقاط البيع والشبكة الوطنية وأنظمة الوزارات. أعطال التكامل نادراً ما كانت نظيفة: تنتهي مهلة العملية في المنتصف فيختلف الطرفان على ما حدث. لذلك كان العمل تسجيلاً ومطابقة واختبار قبول بحالات حقيقية ومورّدين يصلحون من جهتهم.
